### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autosomal dominant nocturnal frontal lobe epilepsy 5  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.799)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:18865)

**Proposed mechanism:** Gain-of-function mutation in KCNT1 (HGVS:c.1709G>A) —DISRUPTS→ KCNT1 (HGNC:18865); KCNT1 (HGNC:18865) —INCREASES→ Neuronal excitability (GO:0007274); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007274) —LEADS_TO→ Seizures (HP:0001250); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007274) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); Neuronal excitability (GO:0007274) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy, nocturnal frontal lobe (HP:0011351). Gain-of-function mutations in KCNT1 lead to increased neuronal excitability, manifesting as seizures, intellectual disability, and nocturnal frontal lobe epilepsy.

**How to falsify it:** The presence of a common, well-established loss-of-function variant in KCNT1 with a high allele frequency (>1%) in gnomAD that is associated with either disease would refute the proposed gain-of-function mechanism. _(variant: rs749301538)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting KCNT1 channel activity could offer a unified therapeutic strategy for both Mala--Plumley-Pingault syndrome and autosomal dominant nocturnal frontal lobe epilepsy 5, potentially through channel blockers or modulators.
